notes.meaning: Children are told to obey their parents because they belong to the Lord. Doing this is right and fair in God's eyes, as long as what parents ask honors him. It shows that learning to follow God begins with showing respect in the home.

Paul quotes the fifth commandment, which commands children to honor both father and mother. Honoring means treating parents with love, respect, and practical care. This was the first rule in the Ten Commandments that came with a specific promise attached to it.

The promise linked to the commandment is that life will go well and be prolonged on the earth. While God gave this to ancient Israel about living in Canaan, it stands as a general truth that honoring parents brings God's blessing. Learning respect early in life protects a person from many painful troubles.

Fathers are warned not to treat their children harshly or make them angry with unfair demands. Instead, parents are called to raise their children with gentle discipline and teaching that points them to the Lord. Christian parenting guides children with patient love rather than harsh anger.

Slaves in the Roman world are told to obey their earthly masters with deep respect and an honest heart. They were to view their daily work as service rendered directly to Christ himself. When we do our everyday duties for Jesus, even hard labor gains dignity and purpose.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Scholars observe that Paul adapts a standard ancient household code, reshaping traditional social rules by placing every relationship under the lordship of Christ and mutual submission.

notes.meaning: Believers are not to work hard only when the master is watching, just to win human praise. Instead, they should see themselves as servants of Christ who carry out God's will with all their heart. True Christian service is just as faithful when no human eyes are looking.

Slaves are urged to serve cheerfully and with good will, viewing the Lord as the real Master they serve. Serving with a good attitude transforms ordinary daily tasks into an act of worship to God. Our work is pleasing to the Lord when it comes from a willing and glad heart.

Every person will receive a reward from the Lord for whatever good they have done, whether they are a slave or free. Earthly masters might fail to notice or reward hard work, but God keeps track of everything. The Lord treats everyone fairly and promises to repay faithful service in eternity.

Christian masters are told to treat their slaves with the same kindness and integrity, giving up the habit of making threats. They must remember that both master and slave answer to the very same Master in heaven. God shows no favoritism based on human rank or social status.

Paul begins his closing message by urging the believers to find their strength in the Lord and his mighty power. Christians do not fight spiritual battles using their own natural abilities or human bravery. We must depend completely on God's unlimited strength working in us to withstand trials.

Believers are instructed to put on the complete armor that God provides. This full suit of spiritual protection guards every part of the Christian life against the clever traps and schemes of the devil. God gives us everything we need to stand firm against spiritual attacks without backing down.

The real battle Christians face is not against human beings made of flesh and blood. Instead, the fight is against invisible spiritual forces, wicked spirits, and demonic rulers working in the darkness of this world. Understanding who the real enemy is keeps believers from treating other people as their true foes.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: Some modern teachers use this verse to teach that Christians are called to battle evil spirits that rule over specific geographic cities or territories.

notes.meaning: Because these evil forces are so dangerous, believers must take up God's full armor right now. Wearing this armor prepares a person to resist and hold their ground whenever a time of fierce temptation or trouble strikes. When the battle is over, the faithful soldier of Christ will still be standing victorious.

A soldier stands firm by putting on the belt of truth, which keeps everything secure and ready for action. Truth means holding firmly to God's gospel and living with honest, sincere hearts. The breastplate of righteousness guards the vital areas, pointing to a life of moral goodness and the righteousness God gives to believers.

Believers must strap on footwear that gives them the readiness that comes from the good news of peace. Just as a soldier needs good shoes to march and stand without slipping, Christians need the inner peace of the gospel to walk firmly through difficult times. Knowing we have peace with God gives us courage to keep moving forward.

Above all the other pieces, believers must take up the shield of faith. In ancient times, large shields covered the whole body and put out arrows dipped in burning pitch. Trusting in God's promises acts like that shield, safely stopping the fiery doubts and sudden temptations shot by the evil one.

Believers are told to receive the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit, which is God's word. The helmet protects the mind with the sure hope and confidence of being saved by God. The sword of Scripture is the weapon the Holy Spirit gives us to turn back the enemy's lies, just as Jesus did when he was tempted.

The spiritual armor must be supported by constant prayer in every season, guided by the Holy Spirit. Christians need to bring all kinds of requests before God, staying watchful and never giving up. We are called to pray not just for our own needs, but faithfully for all of God's people.

differ.view: Praying in the Spirit includes praying in tongues as a special spiritual prayer language given by the Holy Spirit.
Praying in the Spirit means praying with the help and guidance of the Holy Spirit according to God's will, not speaking in tongues.

notes.meaning: Paul asks the Ephesians to pray especially for him so that God will give him the right words whenever he speaks. Even great apostles depend on the prayers of ordinary church members for strength. He wanted the courage to clearly explain the good news of Christ, which had once been hidden but was now revealed.

Paul describes himself as an ambassador for the gospel who is currently wearing a prisoner's chain in Rome. In the ancient world, ambassadors represented kings and were supposed to be protected, not chained. He asks for prayer so that he will not shrink back from preaching fearlessly, exactly as he ought to do.

Paul mentions Tychicus, calling him a dearly loved brother and a faithful servant in the Lord's work. Tychicus was carrying this letter and would give the church a full report about how Paul was doing. Good Christian friends help keep distant churches connected and informed about each other.

Paul sent Tychicus for the specific purpose of sharing news about Paul and his companions so that the believers would not worry. Learning that God was sustaining Paul in prison would bring comfort and courage to their hearts. Christian fellowship brings great relief and encouragement during difficult trials.

Paul prays for peace, love, and growing faith to be given to all the Christian brothers and sisters. These blessings flow directly from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. True spiritual harmony and mutual love come only through the gift of God's grace.

The letter ends with a blessing of God's undeserved favor on everyone who loves the Lord Jesus Christ with an unfailing, pure love. This kind of love is sincere, holy, and lasts forever without fading away. God pours out his ongoing grace on all who remain devoted to his Son.
